author: IGN
description:
Wild Blue Skies reviewed by Will Borger on PC, also available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

"Wild Blue Skies is a decent rail shooter. When it finds the courage to be itself – to separate itself from what inspired it – it occasionally soars. But its slavish devotion to Fox McCloud’s greatest adventure is ultimately its undoing. Too often, it’s simply Star Fox 64 But Worse – worse flying, worse story, worse difficulty tuning – and some of these characters and missions are so similar that they start to border on legally questionable. I don’t think this is malicious. I think these mistakes are born out of a deep-seated love for a game I also adore. Wild Blue Skies wants, desperately, to remind you of Star Fox 64. To make you feel the same things you did when you played it for the first time. But I’ll never be eight years old again, in that room, watching one of my friends do what had, up until that moment, been impossible. You can revisit the past, but you can’t go back in time.
title: Wild Blue Skies Review

description:
For Phantom Blade Zero, the team at developer S-Game is clearly pulling out all the stops in order to bring its bold and exciting vision for kungfupunk to life. By drafting in action movie megastar and martial arts master Donnie Yen to serve as co-producer on its wuxia-inspired action RPG, the Chinese developer is ensuring that every kick, punch, and scintillating sword-slice is delivered with the utmost authenticity and heart-stopping intensity.

In 2025, IGN was fortunate enough to be invited over to S-Game’s Shanghai studio to get an insight into its groundbreaking approach to kung fu motion capture, and to speak with both creative director Soulframe Liang and Donnie Yen himself. It was genuinely spectacular to see Donnie’s team in action, pulling off a breathtaking series of dazzling wirework stunts and daring martial arts moves, but it wasn’t until I saw a stunt performer juggling a baby on the blade of his sword before launching it into the air that I knew I was witnessing somet
